title: Replace Loop with Pipeline

solutions.title: Named pipeline steps, one loop left alone
solutions.tradeoff: Reading the accepted or rejected total now means trusting filter/map/reduce chains under names instead of watching one loop build them, and the capacity check is a hand-written loop sitting next to three pipelines - a reader has to notice why, not assume the exercise ran out of time to convert it.

reviewFocus: Do renderAcceptedSection and renderRejectedSection each read as one filter plus one map, or did the filter predicate grow a second job along the way?
Is acceptedTotalCents computed by folding the already-filtered accepted deliveries, or does it re-check qualityPassed itself - a second definition of "accepted" that could drift from the first?
Does findCapacityBreach still stop at the first delivery that tips the scale, or would a reader's rewrite as reduce() silently keep scanning past it?
Is the capacity check's loop commented with why it stayed a loop, or does it just sit there looking like an oversight next to three pipelines?

Would collapsing accepted and rejected into a single pass with two accumulators (as in the challenge) actually be fewer lines than two filters - and if so, is line count the right way to judge this trade?
